messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Synthetic canary failure spike in eu-west-1 (canary-id: synth-queue-42). 30m failure rate = 38% (threshold 10%) — PagerDuty page fired to #oncall (PD-INC-9302).
Jordan H: acked in PD, jumping on it. pulling logs.
Maya R: ack, on my way. any customer-facing errors reported?
Devon L: quick check: tailing prober logs now. running `kubectl -n prober logs -l app=canary-runner --since=15m`
Devon L: ```
2026-03-15T12:03:02Z synth-runner eu-west-1 http request failed status=502 host=api-euw-1.redwood.internal path=/health  count=42
2026-03-15T12:04:05Z synth-runner eu-west-1 probe timeout cfg=5s target=upstream-router-euw
```
Olivia K: 502s from upstream router look suspicious. Are we seeing increased 5xx in real traffic metrics? Link to dashboard: https://console.redwood/infrastructure/eu-west-1/requests?group=5xx
Jordan H: checking real traffic now — looks like a small rps bump but 5xx rate for customers is ~0.4% at the moment. not widespread yet.
Maya R: good. so canary is failing faster than production. could be a synthetic-specific path or header. does the canary use a different auth token or route?
Devon L: canary uses prober service account + new path /healthv2. I see repeated `connection reset by peer` lines when prober opens many keepalive streams.
Devon L: ```
net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
EOF while reading from socket
```
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-INC-9302 escalated to level2 (oncall: Maya R) — 3 unacked alert(s) consolidated.
Jordan H: I'm going to scale down prober concurrency temporarily to reduce pressure: `kubectl -n prober scale deployment/synth-runner --replicas=1` and patch config concurrency=2
Olivia K: Can we gate canary traffic to a smaller subset instead? Suggest toggling prober fanout to 1 region. Playbook: https://workflows.redwood/playbooks/synth-failover
Maya R: I'll take over the PD handoff. Jordan, do the scale-down and then update the toggle. I'm going to notify SRE and infra because that router (upstream-router-euw) ownership is infra. @InfraPager please triage if router is overloaded.
pagerduty: Notification: PD-INC-9302 acknowledged by Jordan H at 2026-03-15T12:07:10Z. Next escalation if unacked: 2026-03-15T12:17:10Z.
InfraPager (via mention): looking. pulling router metrics + rules. early suspicion: misbehaving rate-limiter that started returning 502 when connection pool exhausted.
Devon L: Jordan applied scale-down and concurrency patch. canary error rate dropped from 38% -> 8% within two probe cycles.
Jordan H: toggled canary fanout to eu-west-1 only (was global) — command: `proberctl set-fanout synth-queue-42 --regions eu-west-1` (temporary)
Maya R: thanks. I'll keep PD acknowledged and monitor for 20m. if infra confirms router pool issues, we'll plan a rollback of the rate-limit rule. Also prepping incident timeline.
Olivia K: Noted. capturing short blameless timeline to share with customers if impacted. No active customer incidents so far, but we'll prepare a canned status message: "We detected elevated synthetic check failures in eu-west-1; internal mitigation in progress. No customer-facing errors observed. We'll update in 30m."
Jordan H: infra reports router pool exhaustion: patching upstream-router config to increase max_conns from 500 -> 1500 and restarting router instances via rolling restart (no downtime).
InfraPager: rolling restart started at 2026-03-15T12:20Z. monitoring CPU and connection metrics.
Devon L: canary failure rate now stable at 0-2%. real customer 5xx remains low.
Maya R: good. I'll hand back to Jordan for postmortem draft and to close PD when we have 30m stable. Taking note for runbook update: add canary fanout kill-switch and prober concurrency default lowered.
Jordan H: creating a short incident note in #incidents-postmortems and a ticket: PM-2456. Link: https://tickets.redwood/PM-2456
Maya R: PD closed at 2026-03-15T12:55Z. leaving followups: infra to add connection pool autoscale check to sentinel; devex to add prober config safety; ops to document rollback steps.
Olivia K: Adding post-incident customer note draft to the ticket. good run. :thumbsup:
Jordan H: closing thread. thanks team.
